episodes.title: Family Cults, Religious Abuse & Coercive Control | Stella McCormick
episodes.description: Can a family function like a cult? For Stella McCormick, the answer became clear only after years of untangling the beliefs, rules, and patterns of control she had been raised to accept as normal. In this episode of The Reconstructing, Katie Grace sits down with Stella, author of Deliver Us from Mother: Faith, Fear, and the Family Cult That Broke Me, to explore the intersection of religious trauma, childhood abuse, and coercive control within family systems. Stella shares her experience growing up in a high-control, fundamentalist Christian household where abuse was framed as biblical discipline, individuality was discouraged, and secrecy and fear kept the family isolated. She discusses the process of recognizing what had happened to her and her siblings, making the difficult decision to report her parents to CPS, and navigating the guilt and grief of going no contact. Together, Katie and Stella unpack seven characteristics of cultic family dynamics, the lasting impact of having a controlling parent's voice internalized, and the ongoing work of rebuilding self-trust, recognizing your own accomplishments, and learning that you are inherently worthy. Content note: This episode includes discussion of childhood abuse and neglect, sexual assault, suicidal ideation, and other potentially distressing topics. Please listen with care and use your discretion.
